correctness.rationale: PASS: The Petersen graph is KG(5,2) on ten two-subsets, its 15 graph edges are disjointness pairs, and its ordinary matching-complex simplex counts in dimensions 0..4 are exactly (15,75,145,90,6). Independent exact rational elimination of all cyclic orientation-signed invariant chain complexes for the seven S5 conjugacy classes returned boundary-rank rows [(14,61,79,6),(8,28,39,3),(8,29,37,4),(4,21,27,2),(2,10,13,1),(4,14,19,1),(2,13,15,2)], yielding invariant (H2,H3) dimensions [(5,5),(1,3),(3,3),(3,1),(1,1),(1,1),(1,1)]. Möbius/element-order inversion of cyclic invariant dimensions gives characters chi2=(5,-3,1,2,0,-1,0)=sign(g)*fixed_symbols(g) and chi3=(5,1,1,-1,1,-1,0)=character of S^(3,2). Independent checks of all 120 signed Lefschetz traces and modular boundary ranks corroborate. In characteristic zero, averaging chain complexes is exact and barycentric subdivision gives rational homology of quotient X/G as G-invariants, which vanish for S5 and yield exactly one H2 for A5. This is an exhaustive finite computation rather than partial search.

value.rationale: PASS: A complete S5 character for both nonzero rational homology groups and the different S5/A5 quotient homologies is a canonical, concrete refinement of a known nonequivariant Petersen matching complex. Such equivariant data distinguish symmetry-invariant cycles that Betti numbers and wedge-of-spheres topology cannot detect, making it an independently meaningful exact finite invariant.

final_claim: For the Petersen graph ordinary matching complex, reduced rational H2 is the sign-twisted five-point S5 permutation module, reduced H3 is the Specht module S^(3,2), other reduced rational homology vanishes, and the S5 and A5 quotients have the stated distinct homology.
limitations: Only rational homology representations of one Petersen ordinary matching complex; no integral equivariant lattice/homotopy theorem.
